A003.quote: La fonte riporta: «Le canal de l’Ourcq est inauguré le 15 août 1813».

A005.title: Canal Saint-Denis: completamento e apertura

A006.title: Canal Saint-Martin: scavo e costruzione (cantiere effettivo)
A006.quote: Nel modello: GRADUALE 1822→1825 (prima pietra 3 maggio 1822, inaugurazione 4 novembre 1825, riga A007). Il 1802 resta solo come nota (legge/progetto). CONFLITTO tra cronologie istituzionali: la Ville de Paris scrive «Les travaux de creusement du canal débutent en 1802 et s’achèvent vingt ans plus tard»; la mairie du 10e indica «Le 3 mai 1822, la première pierre est posée». Il 19 maggio 1802 è anche la data della legge/progetto; inaugurazione nel 1825. Non assimilare automaticamente avvio del progetto e inizio effettivo del cantiere.

A007.title: Canal Saint-Martin: completamento e apertura
A007.quote: La Ville de Paris indica: «Charles X inaugure le canal Saint-Martin, le 4 novembre 1825». È la data d’inaugurazione, distinta dalla posa della prima pietra nel 1822.

A013.title: Canal Saint-Martin: copertura parziale sul boulevard Richard-Lenoir
A013.quote: La mairie du 10e indique : «C’est entre 1860 et 1862 que le préfet Haussmann décida de couvrir le canal au moyen d’une voûte [...] afin de créer le boulevard Richard-Lenoir».

A014.title: Canal Saint-Martin: copertura del tratto tra République e Bastille
A014.quote: La mairie du 10e indique : «Une idée reprise en 1906, avec la voûte du Temple [...] afin de donner le jour au boulevard Jules Ferry».

B001.title: Enceinte de Philippe Auguste — rive droite: costruzione

B002.title: Enceinte de Philippe Auguste — rive gauche: costruzione

B004.title: Enceinte de Charles V: dismissione e demolizione progressiva
B004.quote: La fonte conferma che le due cinte più tarde furono rase sotto Luigi XIV; intervallo operativo approssimativo.

B005.title: Enceinte de Louis XIII: costruzione
B005.quote: Le plan des enceintes porte «enceinte de Charles IX à Louis XIII...1560-1643»; la Ville de Paris date le lancement du front de 1566.

B006.title: Enceinte de Louis XIII: demolizione
B006.quote: La Ville de Paris indique que les deux enceintes les plus tardives sont rasées sous Louis XIV pour laisser place aux grands boulevards; 1670 est le début documenté de cette phase, 1700 borne opérationnelle. Date/fase non sostenuta da una citazione puntuale verificabile nella fonte attualmente associata; mantenere come ipotesi a bassa affidabilità.

B007.title: Mur des Fermiers généraux: costruzione
B007.quote: La fonte riporta: «La construction du mur des Fermiers généraux s’étend de 1784 à 1790».

B010.title: Enceinte de Thiers: demolizione
B010.quote: La fonte riporta che fu distrutta «dans les années 1920»; intervallo reso in anni interi per il modello.

B011.title: Annessione dei comuni suburbani e passaggio da 12 a 20 arrondissement
B011.quote: La fonte riporta che nel 1860 i limiti furono ampliati e gli arrondissement passarono da 12 a 20. Date/fase non sostenuta da una citazione puntuale verificabile nella fonte attualmente associata; mantenere come ipotesi a bassa affidabilità.

B012.title: Boulevard périphérique: apertura al traffico

C001.title: Rue de Rivoli: primo asse urbano
C001.quote: Le document d’urbanisme de la Ville de Paris décrit le prolongement de la rue de Rivoli parmi les percées du Second Empire et indique un segment déjà tracé en 1854; les bornes de cette ligne restent un phasage général à préciser par tronçon. Date/fase non sostenuta da una citazione puntuale verificabile nella fonte attualmente associata; mantenere come ipotesi a bassa affidabilità.

C003.title: Boulevard de Sébastopol: apertura
C003.quote: Paris Musées / Musée Carnavalet indique : «Ce boulevard a été inauguré le 5 avril 1858»; l’inauguration de 1858 est attestée, le démarrage du chantier en 1854 reste une borne de phase.

C006.title: Avenue de l’Opéra: apertura
C006.quote: La notice de Paris Musées indique : «le percement de l’avenue à partir de 1864 (achevé en 1876)»; ouverture et achèvement du percement sont distingués.

C007.title: Boulevard Haussmann: apertura e completamento
C007.quote: Paris Musées documente explicitement «Le percement du boulevard Haussmann en 1926»; cette phase terminale complète les travaux antérieurs.

C008.title: Boulevard Voltaire: apertura
C008.quote: La notice de Paris Musées identifie le boulevard Voltaire sous son ancien nom «boulevard du Prince-Eugène» et date son inauguration de 1862.

C014.title: Place des Vosges: realizzazione e impianto
C014.quote: La Ville de Paris indique : «C’est en 1605 que la place prit le nom de “place Royale”» et «La place Royale ne fut achevée qu’en 1612». Place postérieure à 1190, donc absente de l’état initial.

C016.title: Les Halles: mercato centrale, costruzione dei pavillons Baltard
C016.quote: Paris Musées indique que les pavillons de fer, verre et fonte furent construits «de 1852 et 1870».

C017.title: Les Halles: demolizione dei pavillons Baltard
C017.quote: Paris Musées indique le transfert du marché à Rungis en 1969 puis «leur démolition en 1971-1973».

C019.title: Boulevard Richard-Lenoir: realizzazione sopra il canal Saint-Martin coperto
C019.quote: La mairie du 10e indique : «C’est entre 1860 et 1862 que le préfet Haussmann décida de couvrir le canal au moyen d’une voûte [...] afin de créer le boulevard Richard-Lenoir».

bridges.name: Pont au Change

bridges.name: Petit-Pont - Cardinal Lustiger
bridges.note: A crossing existed in 1190 (page: since antiquity). Swept away by floods at least 13 times 885-1658; rebuilt in stone 1398-1408, again 1409-1416 with houses; collapsed 1649, 1651, 1658, 1659; replaced 1719 without houses; present bridge begun 1852, opened 1853

bridges.name: Pont Saint-Michel
bridges.note: Stone bridge 1379-1387; collapsed 31 Jan 1408 with its houses (gap not modeled); rebuilt 1617-1623; houses stayed until 1808 (order of 1786); present bridge 1857

bridges.name: Pont Marie
bridges.note: Built 1614-1635 (G007, page). Flood 1 March 1658 destroyed 20 houses and two arches; wooden repair 1660, stone reconstruction completed 1670. Houses removed after the 1786 order (Pont Saint-Michel page)

bridges.name: Pont de la Tournelle
bridges.note: Wooden 1620, stone 1654, demolished 1918, present bridge 1928 (Wikipedia). Legacy table had a wooden bridge in 1369.5 (G062 from memory): not confirmed by the page read, dropped

bridges.name: Pont Royal
bridges.note: Wooden Pont Sainte-Anne / Pont Rouge 1632 (repaired 1649, rebuilt 1651 and 1660, burnt 1654, carried away later); stone bridge 25 Oct 1685 - 13 Jun 1689 (completed 1689.45); last reconstruction 1850

bridges.name: Pont des Arts
bridges.note: First metal bridge in Paris, pedestrians, 1802-1804. Partial collapse in 1979 (barge), present bridge built 1981-1984, inaugurated 27 June 1984

bridges.name: Pont de la Concorde

title: PARIS
1190 TO NOW

cards.title: A wall for Paris
lines: Philippe Augustus orders a stone wall before leaving on crusade.

cards.title: Notre-Dame rises
lines: The choir is done; the nave goes up next.

cards.title: The Louvre fortress
lines: A castle guards the wall where it meets the Seine.

cards.title: The Left Bank wall closes
lines: About 253 hectares inside the walls.

cards.title: 50,000 Parisians
lines: Already one of the largest cities in Europe (estimate).

cards.title: Sainte-Chapelle
lines: A royal chapel built to hold the Crown of Thorns.

cards.title: ~120,000 people
lines: Estimate; Paris is the biggest city in Western Europe.

cards.title: Notre-Dame completed
lines: Almost two centuries after the first stone.

cards.title: The Black Death
lines: Paris loses a large share of its people (estimates vary).

cards.title: The Bastille
lines: A fortress guards the new eastern gate.

cards.title: The Charles V wall
lines: The Right Bank city doubles behind a new wall.

cards.title: Pont Notre-Dame
lines: A bridge lined with houses.

cards.title: Two kings enter Paris
lines: Henry V of England and Charles VI ride in together under the Treaty of Troyes.

cards.title: The English leave Paris
lines: Charles VII can finally return to a city held by Burgundians and English since 1418.

cards.title: Back to 200,000
lines: The city recovers after the Hundred Years War (estimate).

cards.title: A new Hôtel de Ville
lines: Work begins on the Renaissance city hall.

cards.title: A Renaissance Louvre
lines: The medieval castle starts to become a palace.

cards.title: The Tuileries Palace
lines: Catherine de' Medici builds a palace west of the Louvre.

cards.title: Henry IV takes Paris
lines: The Catholic League held out in the city until 1594.

cards.title: Pont Neuf opens
lines: The first Paris bridge without houses on it.

cards.title: Place Royale
lines: Today Place des Vosges.

cards.title: Pont au Double
lines: The first bridge on the site (1626).

cards.title: The Fossés Jaunes
lines: A new rampart pushes the Right Bank west.

cards.title: Pont Marie
lines: Christophe Marie links Île Saint-Louis to the Right Bank.

cards.title: 450,000 people
lines: Estimate.

cards.title: Île Saint-Louis
lines: Two islets are joined and built over.

cards.title: The Louvre Colonnade
lines: A classical façade facing the city.

cards.title: The walls come down
lines: Old ramparts become the first Grands Boulevards.

cards.title: 500,000 Parisians
lines: Estimate.

cards.title: The Invalides dome is gilded
lines: Mansart's dome: 107 m.

cards.title: Place Vendôme
lines: A royal square of matching façades.

cards.title: 550,000 Parisians
lines: Estimate.

cards.title: Place Louis XV
lines: Today Place de la Concorde.

cards.title: Sainte-Geneviève
lines: The church that will become the Panthéon.

cards.title: Houses cleared off the bridges
lines: Pont Notre-Dame and Pont au Change lose their houses.

cards.title: The Farmers-General wall
lines: A customs wall around the whole city.

cards.title: Pont de la Concorde
lines: A new bridge to Place Louis XV.

cards.title: The monarchy falls
lines: After the insurrection of 10 August 1792, the First Republic replaces the king.

cards.title: 547,756 Parisians
lines: First census.

cards.title: Napoleon, emperor
lines: He is granted the title Emperor of the French on 18 May 1804.

cards.title: The Grand Châtelet is demolished
lines: The medieval fortress at the heart of the Right Bank.

cards.title: Arc de Triomphe
lines: Napoleon orders a triumphal arch at the Étoile.

cards.title: The Rohan wing
lines: The Louvre grows along the new Rue de Rivoli.

cards.title: Canal de l'Ourcq
lines: Fresh water reaches La Villette.

cards.title: The kings return
lines: In April 1814 the allied armies restore Louis XVIII.

cards.title: Canal Saint-Denis
lines: The canal is completed (1821).

cards.title: The Ourcq canal is complete
lines: From Mareuil to Paris.

cards.title: Canal Saint-Martin
lines: A canal brings water and barges into Paris.

cards.title: Pont de Grenelle
lines: The first bridge on the site opens on 1 May 1827.

cards.title: Three new crossings
lines: Arcole footbridge and Pont de l'Archevêché.

cards.title: The July Revolution
lines: Three days of fighting end the Bourbon Restoration.

cards.title: Pont Louis-Philippe
lines: The king lays the first stone.

cards.title: Pont du Carrousel
lines: A bridge straight into the Louvre.

cards.title: The Arc is finished
lines: Thirty years after the first stone.

cards.title: Île Louviers disappears
lines: Its river arm is filled; the island joins the Right Bank.

cards.title: The Thiers wall
lines: A 33 km fortification around Paris.

cards.title: Over 1 million
lines: 1,053,897 Parisians.

cards.title: A second Napoleon
lines: Louis-Napoleon proclaims himself Emperor on 2 December 1852.

cards.title: Haussmann begins
lines: Boulevards are cut straight through the old city.

cards.title: Pont des Invalides
lines: The suspension bridge is replaced in stone.

cards.title: Les Halles
lines: Baltard's iron and glass market pavilions.

cards.title: Boulevard de Sébastopol
lines: Inaugurated through the heart of the Right Bank.

cards.title: A new spire for Notre-Dame
lines: Viollet-le-Duc's spire is inaugurated.

cards.title: 20 arrondissements
lines: On 1 January 1860 Paris annexes its suburbs up to the Thiers wall.

cards.title: Pont au Change
lines: Rebuilt as it stands today.

cards.title: The canal goes underground
lines: Boulevard Richard-Lenoir is built on top.

cards.title: The New Louvre
lines: The Louvre finally joins the Tuileries.

cards.title: The empire collapses
lines: After Sedan, the Third Republic is proclaimed on 4 September 1870.

cards.title: The Commune
lines: The Tuileries and the Hôtel de Ville are set on fire.

cards.title: Palais Garnier
lines: The opera house opens.

cards.title: Avenue de l'Opéra
lines: Cut straight from the Louvre to the Opéra.

cards.title: A new Hôtel de Ville
lines: Rebuilt on the same site.

cards.title: Tuileries demolished
lines: The burnt palace is cleared away.

cards.title: Eiffel Tower opens
lines: 300 m: the tallest structure in the world.

cards.title: Pont Alexandre III
lines: A single steel arch over the Seine.

cards.title: World Fair and the first Métro line
lines: Grand Palais, Pont Alexandre III, Line 1.

cards.title: Pont de Bercy
lines: Widened 5.5 m to carry the Métro.

cards.title: Voûte du Temple
lines: Another stretch of the canal is covered.

cards.title: The great flood
lines: The Seine rises more than 8 m.

cards.title: Sacré-Cœur completed
lines: Consecrated only in 1919, after the war.

cards.title: 2.9 million Parisians
lines: The all-time peak.

cards.title: Boulevard Haussmann
lines: Finished 69 years after it began.

cards.title: The Thiers wall is razed
lines: Its belt becomes housing and, later, the Périphérique.

cards.title: 2,891,020 Parisians
lines: Census.

cards.title: A new Pont du Carrousel
lines: The current bridge opens.

cards.title: Paris is occupied
lines: German armies enter the city unopposed on 14 June 1940.

cards.title: Paris is liberated
lines: The German garrison surrenders the capital on 25 August 1944.

cards.title: 2,725,374 Parisians
lines: The first census after the war.

cards.title: 2,850,189 Parisians
lines: Census.

cards.title: La Défense
lines: A business district rises west of Paris.

cards.title: A new republic
lines: The Fifth Republic is established on 4 October 1958.

cards.title: 2,590,771 Parisians
lines: Families leave for the suburbs.

cards.title: Les Halles demolished
lines: Baltard's pavilions are torn down.

cards.title: Tour Montparnasse
lines: 210 m: a tower Paris will never repeat inside the city.

cards.title: Boulevard Périphérique
lines: The ring road is completed.

cards.title: Centre Pompidou
lines: Pipes and escalators on the outside.

cards.title: The Louvre Pyramid
lines: And the Grande Arche at La Défense.

cards.title: Pont Charles-de-Gaulle
lines: Built between 1993 and 1996.

cards.title: 2,125,246 Parisians
lines: The smallest population in a century.

cards.title: Passerelle Simone-de-Beauvoir
lines: Inaugurated in 2006.

cards.title: 2,249,975 Parisians
lines: A brief rebound.

cards.title: Notre-Dame burns
lines: The spire and the roof are lost.

cards.title: Notre-Dame reopens
lines: The spire is back.

cards.title: Paris today
lines: 2,065,560 people inside the city.
